title: Getting around
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: ONE CONTRAST DOES ALL THE WORK: v and na take the ACCUSATIVE for motion and the PREPOSITIONAL for location. Ya idú v magazín is going; Ya v magazíne is being there, which is L1-M7's own sentence. For an inanimate masculine noun the accusative is identical to the nominative, so half of this costs nothing — it is the feminine that shows the move, v Moskvú against L1-M1's v Moskvé. The question words fork the same way: gde asks where a thing IS, kudá asks where it is GOING.

RUSSIAN CANNOT SAY "I'M GOING" WITHOUT DECIDING HOW. idtí is going on foot; yékhat' is going by vehicle. An English speaker has never had to choose, and there is no neutral option to fall back on — Ya idú v Moskvú would mean walking there. The other split, between one trip and going habitually, is real and is L3's; nothing here touches it.

TRANSPORT, decided for this course: "by bus" is both na avtóbuse and avtóbusom, and this course teaches na avtóbuse — one preposition and one case the learner already owns from L1-M7's na rabóte, doing a new job. The instrumental proper is L3's and no display in this level uses it. peshkóm comes in as a WORD rather than as a pattern: it is a frozen instrumental, and there is nothing to copy from it.

The directions reuse M1's imperative: idíte, poverníte. do takes the genitive — kak doytí do stántsii — which is M3's case doing a fourth job after absence, amount and "of". Point back rather than learn it again.

metró does not decline at all. It is the first indeclinable noun in the course, and it stays metró in every position: v metró, na metró, okolo metró. Words borrowed with an unusual ending behave this way — kófe is the other one the learner already has.

sentences.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?

words.note: idtí with do- on the front, which adds "as far as". The prefix is why the preposition do follows it and why the whole thing is about arriving rather than travelling.
A preposition taking the genitive — M3's case doing a fourth job after absence, amount and "of". One syllable, so no stress mark.
A metro or small railway station. The big railway terminus is a vokzál, and the two are not interchangeable.

sentences.trap: do takes the genitive, so stántsiya becomes stántsii. That is the same case as M3's Zdes' net magazína — the fourth job it does, and no new ending to learn.
sentences.sound: iz-vi-NI-tye kak day-TI da STAN-tsi-i. The unstressed o of do reduces to a and leans onto the noun.

variations.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the shop?
variations.changed: a masculine noun in the same genitive

variations.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
variations.changed: M1's other opener

variations.cue: How do I get to the street?
variations.changed: no opener — direct, and noticeably barer

mistake.why: do takes the genitive: kak doytí do stántsii?

sentences.usage: Stopping someone in the street. The verb already says you intend to walk.
sentences.mnemonic: do means as far as, and takes the genitive.

words.note: The imperfective imperative of idtí — M1's rule paying off, because directions are a way of proceeding rather than one act.
Straight ahead. It also means "frankly" — Skazhí pryámo, say it straight — which is the same picture in both languages.
Motion to the left. Being on the left is sléva, a different word — Russian keeps direction and position apart here as it does everywhere.

sentences.trap: The imperfective is right here for the reason M1 gave: this is how to go, not one act of going. A perfective imperative would sound like an order to move now.
sentences.sound: i-DI-tye PRYA-ma pa-TOM na-LYE-va. Both final o's reduce to a, so nalévo ends in the same sound as pryámo.

variations.changed: the other direction
one instruction only
turning rather than going — and this one is perfective

mistake.why: Direction takes the na- form: potóm nalévo.

sentences.usage: Giving directions to someone who has stopped you.
sentences.mnemonic: na- on the front means towards.

words.note: A perfective imperative, and correctly so: turning is one act, where going is a way of proceeding. The stress falls on the ní, and the same sentence holds both aspects at once.
nalévo's twin. práva also means "rights" and "a driving licence", which is a coincidence of the language rather than a picture.
Carries a yó, which must be written. The o before the k disappears whenever an ending is added — perekryóstke, not perekryóstoke.

sentences.trap: One sentence, two aspects, and both are right. poverníte is one act; the idíte of the sentence before was a way of going. The choice is about how the action is being presented, never about how long it takes.
sentences.sound: pa-vir-NI-tye na-PRA-va na pi-ri-KRYOS-tkye. The yó takes the stress, as it always does.

variations.changed: the other direction
a different landmark, feminine

variations.cue: Go straight on as far as the crossroads
variations.changed: do plus the genitive again

mistake.why: This na is location, so the prepositional: na perekryóstke.

sentences.usage: The second half of almost every set of directions.
sentences.mnemonic: Turning is one act; going is a way of going.

words.note: From the verb for stopping. A metro station is never an ostanóvka — that is a stántsiya, and the words are not swapped.
Stem-stressed throughout, so the mark never moves. The v is pronounced f before the t.
It never changes shape: v metró, na metró, do metró. The first indeclinable noun in the course after kófe.

sentences.trap: avtóbusa is genitive and means "of the bus", exactly as M3's stakán vodý did. Two nouns side by side in Russian put the second one in the genitive, and the of is the ending.
sentences.sound: gdye a-sta-NOF-ka af-TO-bu-sa. Both v's go voiceless, which is why the word sounds nothing like its spelling.

variations.changed: shorter, and enough when a bus is in sight
the metro, and metró does not decline
an answer rather than a question

mistake.why: The second noun goes in the genitive: ostanóvka avtóbusa.

sentences.usage: The question a traveller asks most, after the one about the toilet.

words.note: Going by any vehicle — bus, car, train, boat. There is no neutral verb covering both this and idtí, so the choice cannot be avoided.
The ya form of yékhat'. It has no obvious relation to the infinitive, which is normal for this small group of verbs.

sentences.trap: This na is the one from L1-M7's na rabóte — location, prepositional — doing the work English does with "by". The course teaches this rather than avtóbusom so that no new case has to be opened for one frame.
sentences.sound: ya YE-du na af-TO-bu-sye. The e of yédu is the ye of "yes", and the stress is on it.

variations.changed: metró, which does not change shape
a different vehicle
on foot, so the other verb entirely

mistake.why: A vehicle takes yékhat': Ya yédu na avtóbuse.

sentences.usage: Saying how you are getting somewhere — asked constantly, and the answer decides the verb.
sentences.mnemonic: Feet take idtí. Wheels take yékhat'.

words.note: The motion twin of L1-M7's gde. English lost this distinction with "whither"; Russian keeps it, and using gde for motion is heard immediately.
The vy form of idtí, carrying a yó and therefore the stress. The whole verb lives on this row: infinitive, ya form, vy form.

sentences.trap: gde and kudá are not interchangeable. Gde vy idyóte? asks where the walking is happening, which is not a question anybody means to ask.
sentences.sound: ku-DA vy i-DYO-tye. Both stresses fall late, which is what gives the question its rising shape.

variations.changed: the vehicle verb
the answer — motion, so v plus the accusative
gde, because nothing is moving

mistake.why: Motion takes kudá: Kudá vy idyóte?

sentences.usage: Meeting someone in the street. It is friendly rather than nosy.

words.note: Going on foot, one trip. L1-M5's poshyól and L1-M6's poydú are this verb's past and future — the family was already the learner's.
The ya form. Russian has no separate continuous tense, so this is both "I go" and "I am going", and only the situation says which.
L1-M7's rabóta in the accusative — the shape a feminine noun takes after a preposition of motion. Its own row pointing back, because an L1 file is never edited.

sentences.trap: magazín is an inanimate masculine, so its accusative looks exactly like its nominative. Nothing visible has happened — and the case is still accusative, which is why the feminine version below looks so different.
sentences.sound: ya i-DU v ma-ga-ZIN. The v has no vowel of its own and simply attaches to the front of the next word.

variations.changed: feminine, so the accusative shows: rabótu against L1-M7's rabóte
no motion, so the prepositional — L1-M7's own sentence
domóy is its own word for motion homewards

mistake.why: Motion takes the accusative: Ya idú v magazín.

sentences.usage: Answering kudá, or explaining where you are off to.
sentences.mnemonic: Motion accuses. Location sits in the prepositional.

words.note: A flat word, like M1's núzhno and mózhno, so it never agrees with anything. Éhto dalekó is a complete sentence.
dalekó's opposite, and flat in the same way. Ryádom means the same thing and is warmer — right next door rather than merely close.
Closer than blízko, and the ordinary answer when something is within sight. It is a frozen instrumental, like peshkóm, and nothing is to be copied from its ending.

sentences.trap: Éhto here is the flat pointing word from M2 and agrees with nothing, which is why the same sentence works whatever is being asked about.
sentences.sound: EH-ta da-li-KO i-li BLIS-ka. dalekó is stressed at the very end, and its two unstressed vowels almost disappear.

variations.changed: the shortest form of the question
the answer
the warmer word, with a named thing

mistake.why: There is no yó in this word: dalekó.

sentences.usage: The follow-up to every set of directions, and it decides whether you walk.
sentences.mnemonic: Flat words never agree with anything.

sentences.cue: Is this a street or a square?

words.note: Feminine and regular. Na úlitse means both "in the street" and "outdoors", which is why it is heard about the weather.
Feminine despite ending in a consonant plus a soft sign — the same shape as M2's mat' and doch', and the same warning: the ending does not say the gender.
Plain "or". It is unstressed in speech and leans on the word before it, so it is easy to miss in a question.

sentences.trap: plóshchad' is feminine and úlitsa is feminine, but for different reasons: one ends in -a and the other in a soft sign. Only the first of those is a rule.
sentences.sound: EH-ta U-li-tsa i-li PLO-shchat'. The shch is one long soft sound, not two.

variations.changed: an answer, with M3's adjective agreeing as feminine
a question about place, so gde

variations.cue: The stop is in the street
variations.changed: location, so the prepositional

sentences.usage: Working out where you are from a sign or a map.
sentences.mnemonic: A soft sign hides the gender. Learn the word.

sentences.display: Ya yédu na mashíne, ne na póyezde
sentences.script: Я еду на машине, не на поезде
sentences.cue: I'm going by car, not by train
sentences.literal: I go-by-vehicle on car, not on train

words.note: Feminine, so the na form ends in -e. It also means "machine" in general, which is where the word comes from.
Masculine, with an irregular plural in -á that takes the stress off the stem. The singular is stem-stressed throughout.
A word rather than a pattern. Its -om ending is a frozen instrumental — the case this level does not open — and nothing else in the module is built the same way.

sentences.trap: Both halves take na plus the prepositional, and the ne only denies the second. The frame is not repeated because the verb is not repeated.
sentences.sound: ya YE-du na ma-SHY-nye nye na PO-yez-dye. The shi of mashíne is hard, so it sounds shy and not shee.

variations.changed: the first half alone

variations.display: Ya idú peshkóm, ne na avtóbuse
variations.script: Я иду пешком, не на автобусе
variations.cue: I'm walking, not going by bus
variations.changed: on foot, so idtí — and peshkóm takes no preposition
a question, and the vy form

mistake.display: Ya yédu na mashínu, ne na póyezde
mistake.script: Я еду на машину, не на поезде
mistake.why: This na is means, not motion, so the prepositional: na mashíne.

sentences.usage: Arranging how to travel, and correcting an assumption about it.
sentences.mnemonic: By vehicle: na plus the prepositional, every time.
